options.title: Shut the Strait of Malacca. Where do tankers go?
options.first_line: Shut the Strait of Malacca, the lane of sea between Malaysia and Sumatra. Where do all the tankers go?
options.first_frame: The Strait of Malacca on the old map, a line of tankers sailing through it, and a hand with an eraser starting to rub the lane out.

options.title: The Strait of Malacca closes. Which way round?
options.first_line: The Strait of Malacca closes overnight. Which way do the oil tankers go now?
options.first_frame: A red barrier drops across the narrow end of the Strait of Malacca near Singapore, tankers piling up behind it.

options.title: Malacca Strait blocked: the long way round?
options.first_line: Block the Strait of Malacca and the oil heading to China has to find another way. How long is the detour?
options.first_frame: Tankers sailing toward the Strait of Malacca as it fades from the map, a question mark over the islands of Indonesia.

why: The first frame alone tells the story without sound (a barrier dropping across the strait, tankers piling up behind it), and the line poses a concrete question about where the oil goes without hinting at the answer, while A's eraser is more abstract and C's 'long way round' detour framing gives part of the answer away.
